You said:You

I need you to explain to me how the pathlib library works

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

pathlib is a built-in Python library that helps you work with file and folder paths.

Instead of manually combining strings to create paths, pathlib gives you objects and methods to manage them.

1. Importing pathlib

Python
from pathlib import Path

Path is the main class you'll use.

2. Creating a path

Python
from pathlib import Path

file = Path("data/students.csv")

This creates a path object pointing to students.csv inside the data folder.

Important: It doesn't create the actual file. It only represents its location.

3. Getting information about a path

Python
file = Path("data/students.csv")

print(file.name) # students.csv
print(file.stem) # students
print(file.suffix) # .csv
print(file.parent) # data

Attribute

What it returns

.name

Complete filename

.stem

Filename without extension

.suffix

File extension

.parent

Parent directory

4. Checking whether something exists

Python
file = Path("data/students.csv")

print(file.exists())
print(file.is_file())
print(file.is_dir())

  • .exists() checks whether the path exists.

  • .is_file() checks whether it's a file.

  • .is_dir() checks whether it's a directory.

5. Creating directories

Python
folder = Path("data/students")

folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

  • mkdir() creates a directory.

  • parents=True creates missing parent directories.

  • exist_ok=True prevents an error if the directory already exists.

6. Reading and writing files

You can also use pathlib to read and write file contents.

Writing:

Python
file = Path("students.txt")

file.write_text("Divin\nJohn\nPeter")

Reading:

Python
content = file.read_text()

print(content)

You don't need to use open() for these simple operations.

7. Combining paths

This is one of the most useful features.

Python
folder = Path("data")
file = folder / "students.csv"

print(file)

Output:

Plain text
data/students.csv

Notice this:

Python
folder / "students.csv"

The / operator combines paths. You don't need to manually concatenate strings.

8. Finding files inside directories

Python
folder = Path("data")

for file in folder.iterdir():
print(file)

This lists the immediate contents of the data directory.

To find all CSV files recursively:

Python
for file in Path("data").rglob("*.csv"):
print(file)

Quick summary

Method / Attribute

Purpose

Path()

Create a path object

.name

Get filename

.stem

Get filename without extension

.suffix

Get extension

.parent

Get parent directory

.exists()

Check existence

.is_file()

Check if file

.is_dir()

Check if directory

.mkdir()

Create directory

.read_text()

Read a text file

.write_text()

Write to a text file

.iterdir()

List directory contents

.rglob()

Search recursively

The main idea: pathlib makes working with files and directories easier, cleaner, and more reliable than manually manipulating file-path strings.

Official documentation: Python pathlib documentation.
